intro: Cards, board games, bets and parties: the vocabulary of play.

palabras.consejo: The Spanish deck has forty cards and four suits: oros, copas, espadas and bastos.
It comes from «baraja». You also say «barajar posibilidades»: weighing several options.
With cards, you deal them at the start. It is regular: «reparto», «repartes». The noun is «el reparto».

palabras.significado: game (one round of cards or a board game)
palabras.consejo: A «partido» is a sports match; a «partida» is of cards, chess or video games.
It comes from «tabla». The chessboard has sixty-four squares.
In parchís each player moves four counters. «Ficha» is also a card with data.
It has six faces. You «tira el dado». «Dado» is also the participle of «dar».
You respect the turn: first one, then another. At work there are morning or afternoon shifts.
It works like «gustar»: «me toca», «te toca», «le toca». You ask: «¿A quién le toca?».
You say «hacer trampa» or «hacer trampas». Whoever does it is a «tramposo».
The o becomes ue: «apuesto», «apuestas». «Te apuesto un helado a que gana».
The accent on the i separates the vowels: lo-te-RÍ-a. «Tocar la lotería» is to win it.
It is the same in singular and plural: «un rompecabezas», «dos rompecabezas». Break + heads.
You say «disfrazarse de pirata». The noun is «el disfraz». It takes «se».
«Echar una partida» means to have a game. Stress on CHA.
The j sounds like «h». The verb is about mixing cards.
«Apostar» changes o to «ue»: apuesto, apuestas.
«Yo gano» is the first person of «ganar». Stress on GA.
«Hacer trampas» is to cheat. Feminine plural.
Participle with -ido. «Esconder» changes o to «ue» in the present.
The -ía ending is the conditional. Stress on RI.
Past participle of «barajar». The j is strong, like «h».
Used in conditional sentences: «si hubiéramos jugado».
With «haber», it forms the perfect: «hemos jugado».
Masculine: «el faro». Stress on FA.
The h is silent. The e and a are separate: u-ME-a.
Plural of «torpe». The stress is on TOR.
Plural of «barajar». The j sounds like «h».
«Repartir» means to share out. Stress on PAR.
«Tirar» means to throw or to pull. Stress on TI.
Masculine: «el grito». Its plural is «gritos».
«Al anochecer» means at dusk. The c before e sounds like «th».
«Sacar» means to take out. The c before a sounds like «k».
The accent on ú separates the vowels: ba-UL.
«Disfraz» is singular, plural «disfraces».
«Disfrazarse de» means to dress up as.
Used for men and women: «el pirata», «la pirata».
The ñ sounds like «ny». The stress is on NYWE.
Feminine, but starts with «a» stressed, so it is «la espada».
«Salir» is to go out. Stress on SA.
«Florecer» is to bloom. Also used for things that appear and spread.
The j sounds like «h»: re-FLE-ha.
Third person of «repartir». Stress on PAR.

texto:
**Three words.** A **juego** is the game in general: chess is a juego. A **partida** is one round of cards, chess or a video game. A «partido» is a sports match.

**Cards.** You **baraja** (shuffle), **reparte** (deal) and throw a card. The Spanish deck has forty cards.

**Board games.** On the **tablero** you move the **fichas** after throwing the **dado**. There are chess, draughts and parchís.

**Turns.** You say **tocarle a alguien**, like «gustar»: **¿A quién le toca? Me toca a mí.** It is also used for prizes: **le ha tocado la lotería**.

**Rules.** You must follow them. Whoever breaks them **hace trampas** (cheats) and is a «tramposo».

**Chance.** The **lotería** is a game of chance. **Apostar** is putting money on a result: **te apuesto un euro a que gana**.

**Fun.** A thousand-piece **rompecabezas**, a costume party, a night out. At a party you can **disfrazarse de** pirate. And at the end, the fireworks.

To talk about something in the past that **did not happen**, use **si** + **hubiera** + participle, and in the other part the **conditional**: **Si hubieras barajado bien, no habríamos perdido.** The order can be changed: **No habríamos perdido si hubieras barajado bien.**

For something unreal in the present use **si** + imperfect subjunctive + conditional: **Si tuviera suerte, ganaría la lotería.**

The conditional is never put right after **si**.

ejemplos.estudio: Si hubieras barajado bien, no habríamos perdido.
ejemplos.alumno: If you had shuffled well, we would not have lost.
analisis: Si hubieras barajado bien no habríamos perdido

ejemplos.estudio: Si tuviera suerte, ganaría la lotería.
ejemplos.alumno: If I were lucky, I would win the lottery.
analisis: Si tuviera suerte ganaría la lotería

ejemplos.estudio: Habríamos terminado antes si hubiéramos jugado sin trampas.
ejemplos.alumno: We would have finished earlier if we had played without cheating.
analisis: Habríamos terminado antes si hubiéramos jugado sin trampas

pregunta.texto: What do you do with the cards before dealing them?

opciones.explicacion: Yes: shuffling is mixing the cards before dealing them.
You throw the dice, not the cards, before starting.
You bet money or something else, not the cards.

pregunta.texto: Which form of «tocar» completes the sentence?

opciones.explicacion: Yes: «tocarle a alguien» is in the third person: «te toca».
«Tocas» would be «tú tocas»; here the verb does not agree with «tú».
«Tocan» is plural, but the turn is just one.

frase.texto: La abuela reparte las cartas a todos

piezas.traduccion: Grandmother deals the cards to everyone

pregunta.texto: What does «Me ha tocado la lotería» mean?

opciones.texto: Es mi turno de comprar un billete
opciones.explicacion: Here «tocar» is not about turns but about a prize.

opciones.texto: He ganado un premio de la lotería
opciones.explicacion: Yes: with a prize, «tocar» means winning by luck.

opciones.texto: He tocado un billete de lotería
opciones.explicacion: It is not about touching with the hand, but about winning.

pregunta.texto: Write in Spanish: «the die» (a single dice).

opciones.explicacion: An «a» is missing before it: you say «apostar a que».
Yes: «apostar a que» + verb is the correct form.

pregunta.texto: Which is a game of chance?

opciones.explicacion: In chess you think each move; it does not depend on luck.
A puzzle needs thinking and looking at pieces, not luck.
Yes: in the lottery whoever is lucky wins.
